note: Researched recommendations, written in the site's voice but by somebody who has not been. Opinionated on purpose — a list of facts is not a guide — but every card says plainly that it was researched rather than visited, and a handwritten note in notes.json overrules any of it. This file exists because nothing else can fill it: Wikidata holds three cafes in the whole of Bengaluru and no open dataset in India describes everyday food. See SOURCES.md.
rules: Every record needs a source and a lastVerified date. If it cannot be checked, it does not go in.
Say what to order and when to go. 'Lovely atmosphere' helps nobody.
No opening hours in prose. OpenStreetMap carries them, js/hours.js reads them, and a time written here is a time that rots.
quality and uniqueness cap at 4 here. 5 is reserved for somewhere one of you actually loved.
Always pin `match` with a zone. A chain with fourteen branches will otherwise resolve to whichever one the index happened to list first.

items.title: Vidyarthi Bhavan
items.why: Gandhi Bazaar since 1943, opened to feed students at the National College up the road — Vidyarthi Bhavan means student house. The benne masala dosa is the order and it is fried in enough butter to be a decision. Expect to give your name, wait on the pavement and share a table. Go on a weekday morning; weekends are a different and worse experience.
items.source: Wikipedia; Karnataka Tourism; existence and address confirmed against OpenStreetMap

items.title: Mavalli Tiffin Rooms
items.why: Founded in 1924 by two brothers from Udupi as the Brahmins' Coffee Club on Lalbagh Fort Road, MTR is known for popularising the rava idli. Order that, and the filter coffee.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Koshy's
items.why: A family-run café where Nehru, Queen Elizabeth II and Khrushchev have eaten, and where journalists and writers still gather. Order tea and something off the old menu.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Shree Sagar CTR
items.why: Central Tiffin Room, or Sri Sagar, a Malleswaram restaurant from the 1920s famous for its masala dosa, with or without butter. Get the butter one.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Lalbagh Botanical Gardens
items.why: Hyder Ali's garden from 1760, later run by British superintendents, with a glass house from 1890 that still holds the flower shows around Republic and Independence Days.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Cubbon Park
items.why: The city's central park, officially Sri Chamarajendra Park, named after commissioner Sir Mark Cubbon. Walk it in the morning.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Champaca Bookstore, Library & Cafe
items.why: A bookshop run by booksellers who post their own recommendations, with a children's library and a café. Browse, then sit with a coffee.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Blossom Book House
items.why: A bookshop with shelves across almost every subject, from fiction and history to Kannada novels and author-signed copies. Give yourself an hour.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Toit
items.why: The Indiranagar brewpub that brews its own range, from Tint-in-Wit to Basmati Blonde and a nitro stout. Order a taster of the house beers.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Ulsoor Lake Park
items.why: Ulsoor Lake, one of the city's biggest lakes, near MG Road, spread over fifty hectares with several islands. Walk the edge at sunset.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap
items.imageCredit: Ramesh NG from Bangalore, INDIA · CC BY-SA 2.0

items.title: City Market
items.why: K R Market, the city's largest wholesale market and one of Asia's biggest flower markets, beside Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace. Go early for the flowers.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Albert Bakery
items.why: A Fraser Town bakery on Mosque Road, founded in 1902 and named after Prince Albert, known for savoury snacks and, during Ramzan, its brain puffs.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters
items.why: A café of the Indian roaster that buys from more than eighty coffee estates and smallholders. Ask what single estate is on the bar.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Brahmin's Coffee Bar
items.why: A Basavanagudi tiffin bar from 1965, one of the old vegetarian eating houses that came before the city's darshinis. Stand at the counter for idli, vada and coffee.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Lavonne Café
items.why: The café of Lavonne, a baking and pastry academy teaching since 2012, so the pastries are the point. Come for breakfast.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Kopitiam Lah
items.why: India's first kopitiam, a Malaysian coffee shop and eatery in the tradition of Malaysia's old coffee houses. Order a kopi.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Yauatcha
items.why: The Bengaluru branch of the Soho dim sum teahouse, in MG Road Mall, open all day. Order dim sum and something from the patisserie.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Malgudi Mylari Mane
items.why: A Karnataka restaurant serving traditional vegetarian and non-vegetarian food, with branches in Koramangala and on the Mangalore highway.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Bier Library
items.why: A Koramangala brewpub built around its own craft beer and a comfortable room. Order a flight.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Pizza 4P's
items.why: The Indian branch of Pizza 4P's, the pizza restaurant that began in Vietnam. Order a pizza to share.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: KOKO
items.why: An Asian gastropub with branches in Mumbai and Hyderabad, and a bar in its Bengaluru room. Book for dinner and cocktails.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Arbor Brewing Company
items.why: India's first American craft brewery, opened in 2012 and one of the breweries the city's beer scene is known for. Ask what is new on tap.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: 6oz Coffee and Roasters
items.why: A neighbourhood specialty coffee shop on Tank Road, Ulsoor, pouring espresso drinks, pour-overs and cold brew made with Indian beans.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Krumb Kraft
items.why: A sourdough bakehouse making breads, crackers, cakes and preserves without additives. Buy a loaf.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Amintiri
items.why: A bakery for celebration cakes, loaf cakes and French-style viennoiserie, with a café in HSR Layout. Order a pastry.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Nasi and Mee
items.why: A Southeast Asian restaurant for nasi, ramen, sushi and dim sum. Order a nasi goreng.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Reservoire
items.why: A big Koramangala cocktail bar, opened in 2017 to bring a Manhattan-style cocktail culture to the city. Sit at the bar.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Oota Bangalore
items.why: A restaurant built on hyper-local Karnataka cooking, named after the Kannada greeting 'Oota aita?' — have you eaten? Order across the regions of the state.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Lavonne
items.why: The Whitefield café of Lavonne, a baking and pastry academy teaching since 2012. Come in the morning for pastries and bread.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Lakeview Milk Bar
items.why: An ice-cream parlour that has been part of the city since before Independence. Order a sundae.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters
items.why: A café of the Indian roaster that buys from more than eighty coffee estates and smallholders. Ask what single estate is on the bar.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Rameshwaram Cafe
items.why: A large-format darshini with ordering kiosks, one of the newcomers reshaping the city's standing-room South Indian eateries. Order at the kiosk and eat standing.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Bengaluru Cafe
items.why: A newer darshini with rustic interiors and a more modern look than the old eating houses. Order a dosa at the counter.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Taaza Thindi
items.why: A Jayanagar darshini, one of the newer, rustic-looking standing-room eateries. Order idli, vada and coffee at the counter.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Blue Tokai Coffee Roasters
items.why: A café of the Indian roaster that buys from more than eighty coffee estates and smallholders. Ask what single estate is on the bar.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: The Biere Club
items.why: A brewpub just off UB City inspired by a roomy British pub, with its own beers and food. Order a taster of the house brews.
items.source: the venue's own website; position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Russel Market
items.why: The Cantonment's covered market, built by the British in 1927 and named for municipal commissioner T. B. Russell. Walk the produce and meat halls under the old roof, then out into Shivajinagar's streets.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Yeshwanthpur APMC Market
items.why: The city's biggest wholesale yard for farm produce. This is where Bengaluru's vegetables arrive, so go early, while the trading is on.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap

items.title: Murphy Town Market
items.why: Hoysala Nagara's neighbourhood market, known for its butchers and fishmongers, with one provisions shop, VM Stores, about a century old. One of the old Cantonment markets campaigners fought to save from demolition.
items.source: Wikipedia (CC BY-SA 4.0); position from OpenStreetMap
